WARNING:
The higher sampling rates (44.1 and 48 kHz) enable carrier frequencies above 16 kHz for ultrasonic transmissions. Prolonged exposure to high pitched sounds can damage your hearing, even if you can't hear them.

To be able to decode COFDMTV encoded text messages, Rattlegram Plus Plus needs access to the microphone. Having access to the microphone is considered to be a sensitive permission and you have the right to know what Rattlegram Plus Plus does with that access: The data recorded from the microphone is only used to feed the COFDMTV decoder and spectrum analyzer for the visualization of its frequency content. Rattlegram Plus Plus uses a very small temporary buffer in volatile memory and constantly overwrites that buffer with new data from the microphone. The resulting text message from the COFDMTV decoder is the only data that gets stored in persistent storage on your device.

Encrypted messages, locations, pictures and acknowledgments will show ANONYMOUS on the air. Your call sign is sent inside the encryption, so only stations with the password (and Rattlegram++ 1.2 or later) can see who sent them. Each message loses a few characters to carry it.\n\nOn amateur radio bands, transmissions must identify the station and encryption is generally not allowed. Use this only where it is legal.
